newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand was saved from its weakest point in three months late Thursday after the South African Reserve Bank intervened to assuage frenzied demand for U.S. dollars, dealers said.
"The Reserve Bank knew that the market was very short and had to take dollars back so they came in and gave the whole market," said on dealer.
At 1415 GMT the rand was changing hands at 4.4820/4850 from from 4.4775/4805 late yesterday.
Players were punting on a better day for the rand as morning dollar sales from trickled in from London-based longs and moved the currency to its intra-day high of 4.4750.

But recovery hopes were dashed when one or more sizeable importer orders for the greenback - rumoured to be between $100 million and $400 million - outstripped available supply and sent the rand hurtling toward 4.4900.
Dealers said the unit was saved from a worse beating after the Reserve Bank repeatedly stepped into the market, offering dollar liquidity around 4.49.
For most of the week, the rand has been under a cloud formed by U.S. funds nervous about emerging market currencies mixed with solid dollar demand from local importers.

The rand also stood weaker in cross rate action. It was last at 0.3784/3789 against the German mark from 0.3801/3804 late Wednesday, at 25.8863/9259 yen from 26.4852/5118 previously and 7.3496/3590 to the british pound from 7.3359/3453 before.
Bond market activity was comparatively thin with most players staying square and appearing content to let yields drift in tune with the rand.
"The rand's taken the lead, mainly on trade flows. There was also minimal presence of euro (issuers) today so that didn't give any impetus," said one debt trader.
The key R150 stood at 14.935 percent from 14.930 percent late Wednesday.
Early demand at 14.935 dried up and pushed the yield to 14.96. This was unsustained, however, setting an intraday ceiling for the long bond.
Rand and bond players ignored South African PPI figures showing March's producer price inflation at its highest level in 21 months
March PPI rose 0.1 percent from February to 9.6 percent year on year, figures broadly in line with expectations.
South Africa's money market shortage rose to 7.615 billion rand on Wednesday from 7.493 billion rand on Tuesday, the Reserve Bank said.

Domestic money market rates were little changed from Wednesday with three month NCD rates from major banks stable at 16.40 percent offered, while 90-day BA rates lined up at 14.90 percent from their previous 15.90-95 percent range.
Foreigners were net buyers of 173.91 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after buying 626.01 million rand's worth on Tuesday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal Bond Exchange turnover rose to 7.41 billion rand on Wednesday from 6.24 billion rand on Tuesday.
